title: Oyster Shell Processing Protocol
author: Benjamin Walther
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbd7ii9n
materials: On the computer, open the micromilling software and let it initiate automatic stage calibration. Slide the bar for the “Reflected Light” up to illuminate stage.

The vial headspace is analyzed for CO2 using a ThermoFisher Scientific GasBench II device with a 100 µl sample loop connected to a ThermoFisherScientific Delta V Plus gas-isotope ratio mass spectrometer.

steps.title: Install Saw Blade
steps.instruction: Install the blade on the drive shaft against the inner flange relieved surface.

substeps.instruction: Remove thumb screw, end cap bushing, and outer flange from drive shaft.
Install blade on drive shaft against inner flange relieved surface.
Slip on outer flange and end cap bushing, then hand tighten thumb screw.

steps.title: Prepare Lubricant Pan
steps.instruction: Fill the lubricant pan with de-ionized water and install it in the saw.

substeps.instruction: Lift off the door on the right side of the saw to access the lubricant pan.
Grasp the slide lock knob, pull outward to disengage, lower the lubricant pan tray, and swing it outward.
Remove the lubricant pan and fill with de-ionized water until the blade is immersed by approximately ¼”.
Re-insert the specimen basket into the pan if it was removed.
Replace the full pan on the tray, swing the tray inward to stop, and press the slide lock inward to secure the tray.

steps.title: Mount and Balance Specimen
steps.instruction: Secure the oyster shell in the chuck and balance the support arm.

substeps.instruction: Loosen the set knob and slip the counter balance weight to the rear of the weight shaft to hold the support arm upright.
Clamp the oyster shell in the saddle chuck, cutting as needed to isolate the shell umbo; the final cut must bisect the shell hinge through the umbo perpendicular to growth increments.
Attach the loaded chuck to the support arm using the mounting thumb screw.
Adjust the micrometer head to move the support arm to the far left.
Slide the counter-balance weight toward the front of the unit until balance is achieved and tighten the set knob.

steps.title: Configure Saw Settings
steps.instruction: Set the safety and speed parameters for the cutting operation.

substeps.instruction: Set the thumb screw in the support arm to shut off the saw by depressing the cut-off switch arm upon completion of the cut.
Adjust the micrometer to position the specimen for cutting; apply weight in increments of 25 grams using the four weights (light weights are recommended to reduce surface damage).
Adjust the speed control knob to a setting of 6-7 (200 rpm) while holding the specimen arm by hand above the blade.

steps.title: Perform Sectioning
steps.instruction: Cut the specimen and prepare the final section.

substeps.instruction: Place the blade wiper with the drip lip side down, ensuring brushes contact both sides of the blade and the metal drip lip is not cut.
Press the start button and carefully lower the specimen arm onto the blade to commence cutting.
Once the cut-off switch arm is automatically depressed and the saw stops, remove the chuck from the arm and release the specimen.
Re-clamp and repeat cutting from the configuration steps if necessary until the final cut section (bisecting the resilifer through the umbo) is obtained.

steps.title: Mount Shell to Slide
steps.instruction: Dry and glue the shell section to a petrographic glass slide.

substeps.instruction: Inscribe the sample ID onto a petrographic glass slide using a diamond-tipped etching implement.
Place the sectioned shell on the slide under a laminar flow hood for 24 hours to dry.
Position the dry section in the middle of the slide.
Apply cyanoacrylic glue pen around the entire perimeter of the shell edge to bond it to the slide.
Allow glue to dry for at least 6 hours and verify the mount is secure.

steps.title: Calibrate Micromill
steps.instruction: Set up the mill and calibrate the drill-to-scope offset.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the mill via the back plate switch and power on the computer attached to the video camera.
Affix the slide to the center of the circular plate stage using double-sided sticky tape.
Click “Sample Thickness” on the Setup Checklist and follow the automatic sequence to identify the top of the sample.
Move the drill to a non-analysis test area and drill a small reference hole.
Initiate the “Drill XY Offset” sequence; if the crosshairs in Scope view do not overlap the test hole center, adjust them using the scroll bars and complete the sequence to record parameters.

steps.title: Sample Extraction
steps.instruction: Drill the targeted calcite region and collect the resulting powder.

substeps.instruction: Draw a sample raster in the foliated calcite region just under the resilifer surface, ensuring depth is set to 450 µm.
Blast the sample surface, drill bit, and a platinum weighing boat (after taring it on the balance) with compressed air to remove contamination.
Click “Run Experiment” and ensure “Enable Drill” is checked; monitor the slide for movement during drilling.
Prepare a piece of weighing paper by folding it once lengthwise at a right angle, placing it flat on the table.
After drilling, move the drill to Scope view to clear the sample. Gently lift the slide from the stage by twisting the tape.
Tip the slide over the folded weighing paper, tapping it to shake all powder into the crease.
Transfer the powder from the paper crease into the tared platinum weighing boat.

steps.title: Sample Storage
steps.instruction: Weigh the powder and store it in vials.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the full boat to the balance, close air shields, and record the sample weight.
Tip the powder into wide-mouth 1 dram sample vials (Clear Screw Thread Sample Vials 15 x 45 mm, Qorpak/GLC-00980).
Cap tightly, label with oyster ID and sample position number, and store for shipping.

steps.title: Isotope Analysis
steps.instruction: Process the powdered carbonate for stable isotope ratio analysis (δ13C and δ18O).

substeps.instruction: Dry powdered samples at 60°C in an oven overnight.
Weigh 0.3 mg of dried sample into 12-ml Labco borosilicate exetainer vials (Labco/9RK8W) and cap.
Load vials into a CTC PAL autosampler rack held at 70°C, flushed/filled with helium at 100ml/min for 10 min.
Manually inject several drops of 103% phosphoric acid through the septum into each vial using a syringe.
Return vials to the autosampler rack to equilibrate for 24h at 30°C.
Calculate provisional delta (δ) values using a pure CO2 reference gas and calibrate data on the VPDB scale using standards NBS 18, NBS 19, and LSVEC.
